title: Natural Word Order: Objects, Place and Time
summary: Build clear English statements by keeping verbs next to their objects, placing destinations or locations after the object, and normally putting time expressions after place expressions. Learn when a time phrase can move to the front for emphasis.
learningObjectives: Keep a direct object close to the verb instead of inserting a place, time or manner phrase between them.
Place a destination or location after the object in sentences that have both.
Arrange place before time in a neutral sentence, and move time to the beginning when appropriate.
Edit unnatural word order without changing the intended facts or tense.

explanation.heading: Keep the verb and its object together
explanation.body: When a verb takes a direct object, English normally puts that object immediately after the verb. Do not interrupt the verb–object pair with a phrase such as carefully, yesterday, or at the office. You can usually put a manner phrase after the object instead.
explanation.example: Priya checked the figures carefully before the meeting.

explanation.heading: Put the object before the destination
explanation.body: If an action affects something and also has a destination or location, the common sequence is subject + verb + object + place. This is especially useful with verbs such as leave, put, carry, bring and find. A location phrase should not normally separate a short verb from its direct object.
explanation.example: The technician left the spare batteries in the cupboard.

explanation.heading: Place usually comes before time
explanation.body: When you mention both where an action happened and when, a neutral and widely useful pattern is verb (+ object) + place + time. Time can indicate a date, a repeated schedule, a length of time or a deadline. Keep the whole place expression together.
explanation.example: We reviewed the designs in the conference room on Tuesday.

explanation.heading: Move a time phrase to the front
explanation.body: A time expression can go at the start of a sentence to establish the setting or connect a new sentence to an earlier event. The remaining verb–object–place order normally stays intact. A comma after an introductory time phrase can improve readability, especially when the phrase is long.
explanation.example: Before the interview, Kai revised his notes at home.

explanation.heading: Separate end-position phrases from middle adverbs
explanation.body: Many phrases describing place and time belong towards the end of a clause, but short frequency and attitude adverbs may occupy a middle position close to the verb. Do not use the place–time rule to position words such as usually or probably; those follow separate patterns. Concentrate here on intact objects and clear end-position information.
explanation.example: Our neighbours practise music in the garage every Saturday.

comparisons.title: Object next to verb versus interrupted object

left.label: Natural verb–object sequence
left.note: The object follows answered directly; the manner word follows the object.

right.label: Unnatural interruption
right.note: Immediately separates the verb from its short direct object; put it after the object.

comparisons.title: Neutral place–time order versus fronted time

left.label: Neutral sequence
left.example: The class met in the studio on Thursday.
left.note: The location comes before the time.

right.label: Time set as the topic
right.example: On Thursday, the class met in the studio.
right.note: Moving the time to the start is also natural; the place remains after the verb.

examples.sentence: The courier delivered the documents to reception this morning.
examples.note: Direct object, then destination, then time.

examples.sentence: Riley found an old photograph under the sofa last weekend.
examples.note: The place and time follow the object photograph.

examples.sentence: The visitors watched the demonstration from the balcony for twenty minutes.
examples.note: The viewing location precedes the duration.

examples.sentence: After dinner, I arranged the chairs on the terrace.
examples.note: An introductory time phrase does not separate arranged from the chairs.

examples.sentence: We studied the instructions carefully at the workshop yesterday.
examples.note: The manner word follows the object; location is before time.

commonMistakes.why: Do not put carefully between a transitive verb and its short direct object.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The nurse placed on the desk the form.
commonMistakes.correct: The nurse placed the form on the desk.
commonMistakes.why: With a short object, put the item before its location.

commonMistakes.incorrect: My cousins play at the sports centre tennis every Sunday.
commonMistakes.correct: My cousins play tennis at the sports centre every Sunday.
commonMistakes.why: The short direct object tennis follows play; place and then time follow the object.

commonMistakes.incorrect: We borrowed from our neighbour a ladder.
commonMistakes.correct: We borrowed a ladder from our neighbour.
commonMistakes.why: Keep borrowed and its short object together; the source follows.

studyTips: Underline the verb and circle its direct object; in ordinary clauses, check that the two stay together.
For a sentence with several details, arrange cards in the order action → object → place → time, then read it aloud.
Practise two versions of the same fact: one with time at the end and one with time at the start.

exercises.prompt: Choose the naturally ordered sentence about a training session.
choices: The instructor explained the procedure clearly.
The instructor explained clearly the procedure.
The instructor the procedure clearly explained.
exercises.feedback: A short direct object normally follows explained immediately; the manner word comes later.

exercises.prompt: Choose the natural sentence about a building tour.
choices: We showed to the guests the laboratory.
We showed the laboratory to the guests.
We the laboratory showed to the guests.
exercises.feedback: The object the laboratory follows showed; the destination or recipient expression comes afterwards.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence has a neutral, natural order for object, place and time?
choices: Ava left in the office her coat this morning.
Ava left her coat in this morning the office.
Ava left her coat in the office this morning.
exercises.feedback: Object + place + time is the normal neutral sequence. Time at the end makes the intended order unambiguous.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correctly ordered sentence about a presentation.
choices: Our manager the report reviewed after lunch.
Our manager reviewed the report after lunch.
Our manager reviewed after lunch the report.
exercises.feedback: The direct object the report stays next to reviewed; the time expression follows.

exercises.prompt: Complete with these words in their natural order: left / the parcel / outside the door. The driver ___ before noon.
acceptedAnswers: left the parcel outside the door
exercises.feedback: The object the parcel follows left, and the place follows the object.

exercises.prompt: Complete with these words: in the hall / practised / their speech. The students ___ after class.
acceptedAnswers: practised their speech in the hall
exercises.feedback: The activity has an object, their speech, before its location.

exercises.prompt: Complete using plays / in the garden / every evening. My neighbour ___.
acceptedAnswers: plays in the garden every evening
exercises.feedback: With no direct object, the place comes after the verb and before the time.

exercises.prompt: Complete with saw / a friend / at the library / last night. I ___.
acceptedAnswers: saw a friend at the library last night
exercises.feedback: The object, location and time form a clear final sequence.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence by moving the location phrase after the object: We discussed at the office the proposal yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: We discussed the proposal at the office yesterday.
exercises.feedback: Discussed should be followed by the proposal, not interrupted by at the office.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence by moving only carefully: Rosa finished carefully her assignment.
exercises.feedback: Carefully belongs after the short object her assignment in this neutral wording.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence by moving only yesterday to the end: I left yesterday my backpack on the train.
acceptedAnswers: I left my backpack on the train yesterday.
exercises.feedback: The object and the place remain together; yesterday is moved to the end.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence by moving the object directly after put: They put on the shelf the clean towels.
acceptedAnswers: They put the clean towels on the shelf.
exercises.feedback: Put takes the object the clean towels before its destination on the shelf.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make one sentence using these facts in this order: the courier / placed / the package / at the front desk / this morning. Start with "The courier".
acceptedAnswers: The courier placed the package at the front desk this morning.
speakingExercises.feedback: Keep placed the package together, then say where and when.

speakingExercises.prompt: Reorder these chunks into one sentence. Start with "We": discussed / the budget / in the office / yesterday.
acceptedAnswers: We discussed the budget in the office yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: The object comes after discussed, followed by location and time.

speakingExercises.prompt: Answer in one complete sentence. Where did Ella see my brother yesterday? Facts: Ella saw him at the cinema. Start with "Ella saw my brother" and end with "yesterday".
acceptedAnswers: Ella saw my brother at the cinema yesterday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Say the object before the place and put the time last.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say the corrected sentence only: "The chef prepared carefully the soup." Keep the same facts and begin with "The chef".
acceptedAnswers: The chef prepared the soup carefully.
speakingExercises.feedback: The manner word moves behind the short object.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say one sentence with exactly these facts. She studies; place: at home; time: every Sunday. Start with "She studies".
acceptedAnswers: She studies at home every Sunday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Use place before the recurring time expression.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct this sentence aloud, keeping "yesterday" at the end: "I mailed yesterday the invoice."
speakingExercises.feedback: Do not separate mailed from the invoice.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say two short sentences. Fact one: the team tested the prototype in the lab. Fact two: they reviewed the results on Friday. Start with "The team" and then "They".
acceptedAnswers: The team tested the prototype in the lab. They reviewed the results on Friday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Both sentences keep their verbs next to their objects; each finishes with its relevant detail.

speakingExercises.prompt: Answer in a full sentence: When did Sam return the books to the library? The answer is on Tuesday. Begin with "Sam" and end with "on Tuesday".
acceptedAnswers: Sam returned the books to the library on Tuesday.
speakingExercises.feedback: The direct object the books precedes the destination and time.

listeningExercises.audioText: I sent the application to the training office on Tuesday afternoon.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where did the speaker send the application?
listeningExercises.feedback: The destination follows the object the application.

listeningExercises.audioText: At the weekend, Noah showed his holiday photographs to his relatives in the living room.
listeningExercises.prompt: What did Noah show to his relatives?
listeningExercises.feedback: The photographs are the object of showed.

listeningExercises.audioText: The volunteers packed the supplies in the gym before sunrise.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the exact place-and-time phrase heard after "the supplies".
listeningExercises.feedback: The location in the gym is followed by the time before sunrise.

listeningExercises.audioText: After the concert, we found a lost wallet near the main entrance.
listeningExercises.feedback: The opening time expression fixes when the finding happened.

listeningExercises.audioText: The teacher returned the essays to our class yesterday morning.
listeningExercises.feedback: The class is the recipient of the returned work.

listeningExercises.audioText: Every Friday, Lena checks the equipment in the storage room.
listeningExercises.prompt: Where does Lena check the equipment?
listeningExercises.feedback: The place expression specifies where the repeated check happens.

listeningExercises.audioText: He left his bicycle outside the shop last night.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the exact place-and-time phrase you hear after "his bicycle".
listeningExercises.feedback: The audio says the bicycle was left outside the shop, and gives last night as the time.

listeningExercises.audioText: We printed the tickets at the hotel before dinner.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the exact place-and-time phrase heard after "the tickets".
listeningExercises.feedback: This combines location at the hotel with time before dinner.
